posts.note: Essay on self-driving safety plus a transcribed Hertz call and an interview with the author's daughter Quinn. One own-action intent, two borderline implicit adoption claims, one third-party (Quinn) forecast.
Interview with Erik Won (Wave Neuroscience) on the MeRT FDA clearance for PTSD; the author's own text is mostly present-tense. One own publication expectation, one third-party forecast.
Report on Joe Taylor's AINT trial. The closing call to Congress for coverage of accelerated TMS is advice with no predictive reading and was not logged.
Travel essay; one newsletter content promise and one metaphorical 'Pompeii the week before' hint of upheaval.
Beijing Anding Hospital visit report; one borderline payer claim resting on 'yet'.
Interview with Daniel Kaufmann (Kindbridge). The author's own statements are present-tense impressions; one third-party forecast logged.
Gen-Z slang parody of the Declaration of Independence. 'I will log back in later, bro' is a fictional persona line, not a sincere claim.
Compass Pathways COMP006 Part B press release reproduced with comedic Lil Jon interjections. Six company/third-party forecasts and one hedged author endorsement of the launch timeline.
Personal letter; only the appended Radial video-collection boilerplate carries a forward-looking (procedural) promise.
Radial story-sharing announcement plus news links; one own-organization plan and the same procedural boilerplate.
Essay on suicide prevention. Base-rate statements ('unlikely to die by suicide') were treated as epidemiology, not forecasts.

statements.quote: I’m going to be subpoenaing these records.
statements.context: Transcript of the author's recorded call with Hertz roadside assistance (agent 'Patty') after a hit-and-run in April 2026. The author says he will subpoena the call records because of conflicting statements about whether the damaged rental car was drivable. A later bracketed note says 'the legal back and forth is still going'.
statements.note: Own-action intent stated inside a phone call; repeated as 'That is why I’m going to subpoena this call.' Low forecast value.

statements.quote: what if we could replace drunk drivers with robots? We can.
statements.context: After citing 2024 US crash and drunk-driving statistics (39,254 deaths; 11,904 alcohol-impaired deaths), the author argues that self-driving cars (Waymo) can replace drunk human drivers. Preceded by 'We can’t yet automate men away entirely'.
statements.note: Capability claim with an implicit adoption forecast (robots replacing drunk drivers); borderline.

statements.quote: Even if we divide that in half, it's still better than humans. That's more living beautiful, brilliant younger sisters with an engineering degrees still with us, and less time spending talking to lawyers at car insurance companies.
statements.context: Discussing Tesla's Q1 2025 Autopilot safety report (about 9x safer by Tesla's own numbers) and Waymo/Swiss Re data (92% fewer injury claims). The author claims that even a halved safety advantage means self-driving adoption would result in fewer traffic deaths (reference to Katie Fisher, killed by a driver in 2010).
statements.note: Implicit forecast: wider self-driving use would cut traffic deaths. Borderline; the explicit content is a present comparison.

statements.quote: Yes, but some people would still be against it. ... Some people are loyal to the old ways no matter what.
statements.context: Interview with the author's daughter Quinn about self-driving cars. Asked whether people would like self-driving if it were trusted and proven safer, she says some would still oppose it, comparing them to loyalists in the American Revolution.
statements.note: Daughter's statement; the author credits her 'strangely prescient wisdom' but adopts only 'it's about trust'. Third party.

statements.quote: The pivotal trial data is currently in preparation for peer-reviewed publication.
statements.context: Author's closing note after the interview with Dr. Erik Won (CMO, Wave Neuroscience) about the FDA 510(k) clearance of MeRT (EEG-guided TMS) as an adjunctive treatment for PTSD. States that the pivotal RCT (156 subjects, multi-site, sham-controlled) is being written up for publication.
statements.note: Implicit expectation of publication; Won says in the interview 'it’s in write-up now and we’re moving as fast as we can'.

statements.quote: There is so much coming, including work in the psychedelic space and combination approaches. ... what’s ahead is genuinely exciting.
statements.context: Dr. Erik Won (Wave Neuroscience), asked what PTSD patients should hear, forecasts more treatments coming, including psychedelic and combination approaches; he mentions a just-completed ibogaine combination study whose data he cannot share yet.
statements.note: Third-party (interviewee) forecast; vague. The author does not restate it.

statements.quote: The science we do will turn into a product, and to make it the most scalable product, we have to answer some of these questions. To generate the next, even more scalable product to help the most people, we need to tease these differences apart.
statements.context: After listing the parameter changes bundled into SAINT/SNT (accelerated, fMRI-guided TMS by Nolan Williams), the author states that the research will become a product and that working out which parameters matter is needed for the next, more scalable product.
statements.note: Compound: forecast (science becomes a product) plus a normative need statement. The author offers SAINT at Radial.

statements.quote: Replication with a larger sample, a sham arm, and longer follow-up is the obvious next step. But I think the burden of proof has shifted.
statements.context: Dr. Joe Taylor presenting the AINT trial (40 patients, imaging- vs scalp-targeted accelerated iTBS; about 80% vs 60% response, effect size 0.8) at the Clinical TMS Society annual meeting. He says replication is the obvious next step and that the burden of proof has shifted toward imaging-guided targeting. Reported by the author.
statements.note: Third party; the author endorses the finding ('Nolan was correct that the imaging-based targeting matters') but not the replication step itself.

statements.quote: Before I write about what I've learned at the Summit, which is substantial, but not metabolized yet, I want to share a few observations about China.
statements.context: Opening of a travel dispatch from Beijing, where the author attended a CNS Summit event hosted by Amir Kalali. He promises a later post on what he learned at the Summit.
statements.note: Own newsletter content promise; low forecast value.

statements.quote: It’s a deeply gracious milieu, but with a sense that a rush is about to start for…something. There was a sense of safety on the edge of unease. It’s Pompeii …the week before?
statements.context: Author's impressions of Beijing under the heading 'Things Could Go To $&@! In a Moment.' He describes controlled chaos and surveillance, says 'China seems always on the brink, or brinks?', and compares the city to Pompeii the week before the eruption.
statements.note: Metaphorical, question-form hint of imminent upheaval in China; no concrete event or date. Borderline.

statements.quote: One thing that is similar about the Chinese and American systems of payment is that neither system has figured out how to pay for accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation yet.
statements.context: Visit to the Department of Neuromodulation at Beijing Anding Hospital (about 150,000 TMS patients a year, led by Gang Wang). The author notes that neither China's state insurance nor US payers have worked out how to pay for accelerated TMS (multiple sessions in one day).
statements.note: Present-state claim; 'yet' implies that payment for accelerated TMS will eventually be solved. Borderline forward-looking.

statements.quote: the national helpline number changed, which is going to cause all sorts of confusion as well. ... You’re going to have a slew of people who are calling the wrong number now.
statements.context: Interview with Dr. Daniel Kaufmann (Kindbridge Behavioral Health) on gambling and process addiction. He says the national problem-gambling helpline number changed because of a dispute between the New Jersey Council and the NCPG, and predicts confusion and misdirected calls.
statements.note: Third-party (interviewee) forecast; the author does not comment on it.

statements.quote: Rolling NDA submission and initial review underway and final submission expected to be completed in Q4
statements.context: Compass Pathways press release (July 7, 2026) on 26-week Part B data from the COMP006 Phase 3 trial of COMP360 (synthetic psilocybin) for treatment-resistant depression, reproduced with comedic Lil Jon interjections and the author's comments. Bullet on NDA timing.
statements.note: Company forecast reproduced from the press release. Body text: 'final submission remains on track to be completed in Q4, 2026'.

statements.quote: Commercial launch-readiness on track for end of 2026, with launch expected in first half of 2027
statements.context: Same Compass Pathways COMP006 press release; bullet on commercial launch timing for COMP360 in TRD. The author responds approvingly ('This really is moving quickly!').
statements.horizon_text: end of 2026, with launch expected in first half of 2027
statements.note: Company forecast; the author's response is logged separately.

statements.quote: This really is moving quickly! This seems like a serious team working to make sure they stick the landing on commercialization.
statements.context: Author's reaction to the Compass Pathways bullet 'Commercial launch-readiness on track for end of 2026, with launch expected in first half of 2027'. He signals an expectation that Compass will execute the COMP360 commercial launch.
statements.note: Hedged endorsement of the company's launch timeline; comedic post format, but the comment reads sincere.

statements.quote: Compass anticipates the launch of COMP360 in the first half of 2027 subject to FDA approval and following Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) rescheduling.
statements.context: Body of the Compass Pathways press release. Launch of COMP360 for TRD anticipated in H1 2027, conditional on FDA approval of the rolling NDA (final submission Q4 2026) and DEA rescheduling of psilocybin.
statements.note: Company forecast with conditions (FDA approval, DEA rescheduling). The author only corrects Lil Jon: 'in this context it’s reschedule'.

statements.quote: New 6-month data supports COMP360’s potential to establish a new standard of care in TRD
statements.context: First bullet of the Compass Pathways COMP006 press release: 26-week data (39% clinically meaningful MADRS reduction in the 25 mg arm, durable to week 26) supports COMP360's potential to become a new standard of care in treatment-resistant depression.
statements.note: Company claim; echoed by CMO Guy Goodwin ('has the potential to establish a new standard of care'). Lil Jon's 'okay!' is comedic.

statements.quote: We are convinced this profile will lead to a profound shift in mental health care — moving beyond daily or frequent administration towards an option potentially involving just a few treatments in a year that could be life changing for patients.
statements.context: Quote from Kabir Nath, CEO of Compass Pathways, in the COMP006 press release: COMP360's rapid, durable profile will shift mental health care away from daily medication toward a few treatments per year.
statements.confidence_phrase: We are convinced this profile will
statements.note: Quoted CEO forecast from the press release; the author does not comment on it.

statements.quote: For us, this represents a significant advancement for psychiatry that will strengthen our ability to reduce the suffering and improve the lives of some of our sickest patients.
statements.context: Quote from Tobias Marton, CMO of Mindful Health Solutions, in the Compass Pathways press release, on the COMP006 Part B results for COMP360 in TRD.
statements.note: Quoted clinician forecast; generic. The author's only comment identifies Marton.

statements.quote: If your video is selected to be featured on Radial’s website, social media, or other marketing materials to help others discover TMS, we’ll email to let you know.
statements.context: Closing call for patient and clinician videos for Radial's TMS awareness campaign, appended to the author's open letter to his bipolar disorder. Conditional promise to notify selected contributors.
statements.note: Procedural own-organization promise; near-zero forecast value. Identical boilerplate appears in share-your-story-owen-in-the-news.

statements.quote: So I'm making it possible to share your story more easily. We're starting with transcranial, magnetic simulation, or TMS
statements.context: The author announces Radial's story-sharing program (video collection through vocalvideo links). 'Starting with' TMS implies later extension to other brain medicine treatments. Preceded by the belief that sharing 'is almost certainly an open door to healing for others'.
statements.note: Own-organization plan; implicit expansion beyond TMS. Low forecast value.

statements.quote: If your video is selected to be featured on Radial’s website, social media, or other marketing materials to help others discover TMS, we’ll email to let you know.
statements.context: Radial TMS awareness video call, repeated from the previous post. Conditional promise to notify contributors whose videos are selected.
statements.note: Procedural own-organization promise; near-zero forecast value. Identical boilerplate to an-open-letter-to-my-bipolar-disorder-873.

statements.quote: It would, however, take acknowledging realities like “ready gun ownership everywhere all the time” puts more people at risk of death by suicide, and that's just not the country we live in, here in America, even if it is the case of other places in the world.
statements.context: Section 'Reducing Suicidal Means is Life Saving. We Refuse to Do It.' The author says means restriction is proven and 'We should do more of this', then asserts that America will not acknowledge the firearm-access risk.
statements.note: Implicit negative call: US firearm means-restriction policy will not change. Explicit text is present-tense; the preceding sentence is normative.

statements.quote: we have a whole event series dedicated to them, with the next RAMHT event happening at Psych Congress, on September 14th, 2026.
statements.context: Aside about rapid-acting treatments: the author's RAMHT (rapid-acting mental health treatments) event series will hold its next event at Psych Congress on September 14, 2026; 'Get your tickets now!'
statements.note: Own-organization event announcement; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Let's make getting help for suicide a great customer experience. Then, everyone will want suicide prevention treatment. Because, and I know this sounds outrageous, but having a great experience with a suicide prevention approach would make you more likely to prevent suicide for yourself. You might even recommend suicide prevention to a friend.
statements.context: Closing argument of the essay 'Why is Suicide So Hard to Prevent?': the author proposes that if suicide-prevention care became a great customer experience, everyone would want it and individual outcomes would improve.
statements.note: Conditional forecast contingent on a proposed change; compound with 'would make you more likely' and 'might even recommend'.
